description: Verify that DUT accepts a UDP datagram with Checksum field == 0 (RFC 768 'Fields' — checksum=0 is the legitimate 'no-checksum' opt-out)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 768 lets a sender set Checksum = 0 to skip integrity checking — used historically by latency-sensitive flows that don't want a verify cost. Receivers MUST NOT reject a datagram on Checksum = 0 alone; that's a different code path from 'invalid non-zero checksum' (FIELDS_15). DUT must accept and deliver the datagram.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram with Checksum field set to 0

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester receives the datagram (UT-query confirms)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT delivered the Checksum=0 UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT did not deliver the datagram (treated checksum=0 as invalid)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT accepted the Checksum=0 UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT did not accept the zero-checksum UDP
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for zero-checksum accept
